# 【Standard WEB Ticket Sale】Mark Your Calendar and Let’s Go!

2026.03.13

Thank you for traveling with us!

Standard WEB Ticket for April and May will be on sale from 3pm on March 13 onwards.

Please see the sales details as below.

**Standard WEB Ticket Details**

**１．Sales Schedule**

![](http://www.alpen-route.com/en/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/3e3bd53c01148d1be6ae465d42720ca4.png)

\*Sales schedule for June onwards will be announced when we have details, so stay tuned! Tickets will be on sale usually one month before.

\*The sales schedule is current as of March 13, 2026.

\*Please note that it may be subject to change.

\*We will inform you of the schedule from November 4th onwards at a later date.

**2\. Traveling Sections**

[WEB Ticket Reservation Traveling Sections](https://www.alpen-route.com/_wp/yoyakuweb_kukan)

The last express bus from Ogizawa Station to Nagano Station departs Ogizawa Station at 17:00. Passengers traveling to Nagano should pay attention to the connection time.

**3\. Fare**

Normal fare will be applied to this WEB Ticket and option ticket.

[Fares for individual customers (1-14 people)](https://www.alpen-route.com/en/transport/fare.html)

If you wish to take an express train between Dentetsu Toyama and Tateyama, you will need to pay an additional express fare.

Express fare have changed from April 1st, please visit [“Regarding the Operation of Rapid limited express trains and Revisions to Limited Express Fares”](https://www.alpen-route.com/en/train-express-fares)

**4\. How to Purchase**

This ticket can be purchased only on [WEB Ticket Page](https://tateyama-kurobe-webservice.jp/AlpenTour/html/VW001W0010.html).

\*Cannot be purchased at a ticket counter.

**5\. Others**

[<WEB Ticket> How to Change or Cancel Your Reservation](https://www.alpen-route.com/_wp/webticket_change_and_cancellation)

\*Sales period for June onwards will be anounced when we have details.

**\*Please refrain from making reservations through travel agencies.**

Have an easy, convenient trip with WEB Tickets!

We look forward to your booking! [WEB Ticket Page](https://tateyama-kurobe-webservice.jp/AlpenTour/html/VW001W0010.html)

The Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route (立山黒部アルペンルート) is one of the earliest places in Japan to see autumn color. It begins high up at Murodō (室堂), at 2,450 meters, where the operator says the leaves have peaked around September 23 on average over the past ten years. While the cities are still holding onto summer, autumn has already reached the top of the mountain.

The route spans 1,975 meters of elevation, so the color doesn't arrive all at once. It works its way down over more than a month, from Murodō in late September to the valley around Kurobe Dam (黒部ダム) by mid-October. Choose your week and some part of the route will be at its best.

For peak timing across the rest of the country, see our [**Japan Autumn Leaves 2026: Nationwide Timing Guide**](https://glostravel.com/en/article/japan-autumn-leaves-2026).

> The foliage can change in a matter of days. Don't set your date on the average alone. Check the operator's "Alpine Route News" (アルペンルートだより) right before you leave, then reserve a WEB Ticket time slot and book a room.

* * *

## Peak color, by elevation

![](https://images.microcms-assets.io/assets/c0c22b3f56c344e79706131373dab851/15fea5bed8bf4b109b479670f5290f84/%E7%AB%8B%E5%B1%B1%E9%BB%92%E9%83%A8%E3%82%A2%E3%83%AB%E3%83%9A%E3%83%B3%E3%83%AB%E3%83%BC%E3%83%88%E3%81%AE%E7%B4%85%E8%91%89_%E9%BB%92%E9%83%A8%E3%83%80%E3%83%A0.webp)

The dates below are averages from past years; the operator has not released a 2026 forecast yet. Use them to pick the general week, not the exact day.

| Section (elevation) | Usual peak |
| --- | --- |
| Murodō (2,450m) | mid-Sept to early Oct |
| Daikanbō–Kurobedaira (approx. 1,830–2,316m) | early to mid-Oct |
| Kurobe Dam (1,470m) | around mid-Oct |

Murodō is the first area to turn. The slopes around Mikurigaike Pond (みくりが池) begin to color in mid-September. A little lower, the slopes along the Tateyama Ropeway between Daikanbō (大観峰) and Kurobedaira (黒部平), plus Midagahara (弥陀ヶ原), turn from early October, and the Kurobe Dam valley follows around the middle of the month.

Peak foliage timing varies with each year's temperatures and typhoons, so going by a fixed date can leave you a week early or late. Check the official [Alpine Route News](https://www.alpen-route.com/autumn-leaves/) for the current foliage conditions before you set out.

* * *

## The 2026 season and the November timetable change

The route operates from April 15 to November 30 in 2026, and this year marks the 55th anniversary of the full route's opening.

The lowest sections color latest and can still hold leaves into early November, but the schedule shifts that month too. The regular timetable runs through November 3, and from November 4 to 30 the service switches to a late-season schedule between Tateyama Station (立山駅) and Ōgizawa (扇沢), with fewer runs and earlier final departures. For a late-autumn trip, check the official [timetable](https://www.alpen-route.com/timetable/) and service updates first.

* * *

## Tickets and reservations: WEB Ticket vs. same-day

Traveling the route means transferring between six different vehicles, and how you buy your ticket can make a big difference to autumn waiting times. There are two ways to go: a time-reserved "WEB Ticket," or a same-day ticket bought at the counter.

A WEB Ticket lets you reserve a boarding time at the entry station: the Tateyama Cable Car from Tateyama Station on the Toyama side, or the Kanden Tunnel Electric Bus (関電トンネル電気バス) from Ōgizawa on the Nagano side. For 2026, tickets have been released in stages by travel period since March 13 (from 3:00 p.m.), so check the WEB Ticket page for when your date opens. You must buy by 3:00 p.m. the day before, and there is no same-day WEB Ticket sale at the counter. Each ticket is valid for five days from your reserved boarding time.

Slots are limited, and popular autumn times can fill up early. Same-day tickets are available at the boarding station, but on busy days the operator may limit which sections you can buy tickets for or cap same-day round-trip tickets, and lines at peak hours can run long.

For an autumn weekend, it pays to reserve at least the first leg — the Tateyama Cable Car or the Ōgizawa electric bus — with a [WEB Ticket](https://www.alpen-route.com/webticket/) so you aren't stuck at the gate. To catch the first departure, stay nearby the night before: hotels around Toyama Station, near Tateyama Station, or in Ōmachi on the Nagano side put you on the earliest run. We cover [**getting there from Tokyo — Toyama or Nagano side**](https://glostravel.com/en/article/tateyama-kurobe-access) in a separate guide.

* * *

## Fares for the main sections

Here's what the main sections cost (adult fares, as of February 27, 2026). The full traverse from Tateyama to Ōgizawa is the priciest, over ¥10,000 even one way.

| Section | One way | Round trip |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Tateyama–Ōgizawa (full route) | ¥10,940 | ¥19,680 |
| Tateyama–Kurobeko (Kurobe Dam) | ¥9,140 | ¥16,480 |
| Ōgizawa–Murodō | ¥6,850 | ¥12,300 |

Children's fares cover elementary-school-age kids at about half the adult price, and children under school age travel free. If you ride a limited express on the Toyama Chihō Railway from Toyama Station to Tateyama Station, there is a separate express charge (¥600 for adults).

* * *

## What to wear at Murodō

![](https://images.microcms-assets.io/assets/c0c22b3f56c344e79706131373dab851/a44f22b395794224bdb9410149545c8f/%E7%AB%8B%E5%B1%B1%E9%BB%92%E9%83%A8%E3%82%A2%E3%83%AB%E3%83%9A%E3%83%B3%E3%83%AB%E3%83%BC%E3%83%88%E3%81%AE%E7%B4%85%E8%91%89_%E5%AE%A4%E5%A0%82.webp)

Clothing is the easiest thing to get wrong up here. Murodō sits at 2,450 meters, and it's far colder than the cities below.

The operator's own advice puts autumn temperatures (September–October) around 10°C. From October, snow flurries are possible near 2,500 meters, and temperatures often drop below freezing in November. In 2025, Tateyama's first snow cap of the season was announced on October 29, and Murodō itself already had 10 centimeters on the ground the morning before.

Pack a thick wool shirt or a fleece with a windproof layer over it — a shell or a light down jacket — and bring rain gear even when the forecast is clear, because mountain weather turns quickly. On a day when the city sits in the low 20s°C, plan for single digits at the summit. If you're packing for a wider Japan trip, this is one route where that extra warm layer earns its place in the bag.

> Show up in what you would wear around town and you will be too cold to enjoy the view. Treat a warm outer layer as a must-pack, not a maybe.

Rough weather can suspend service on some sections, so check the official [service updates](https://www.alpen-route.com/diainfo/) before you go and again on the day. The altitude wears you down as well, so take it slowly and rest often.

# Guide to Purchasing Tateyama Kurobe Tickets, Train Tickets, JR Passes, and Booking Ride Times

Latest modified date: 2026-05-28 \| Categories: [Japan Travel](https://www.travelclassroom.net/eng/category/japan-travel)

The previous article introduced various information about visiting [**Tateyama Kurobe**](https://www.travelclassroom.net/eng/tateyama-kurobe.html). This article will continue to introduce how to purchase Tateyama Kurobe passes, train tickets, and JR Passes, including the detailed process of pre-purchasing tickets on the official website and booking ride times for the Tateyama Cable Car and Kanden Tunnel Electric Bus. It will also introduce some JR Passes that include tickets for the Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route transportation and how to use these transportation passes.

![Tateyama Kurobe Pass](https://www.travelclassroom.net/eng/wp-content/uploads/folder01/Alpine-Ticket.jpg)

Table of Contents

## Tateyama Kurobe Passes, Tickets, and Transportation Fees

Visiting Tateyama Kurobe does not require an entrance ticket, but you need to purchase tickets to ride the transportation on the Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route. You can purchase tickets for a single mode of transportation, such as the Tateyama Cable Car from Tateyama Station to Bijodaira, or you can purchase a pass for all transportation on a specific route, such as a pass from Tateyama Station to Ogizawa Station, which allows you to ride the Tateyama Cable Car, Tateyama Highland Bus, Tateyama Tunnel Trolley Bus, Tateyama Ropeway, Kurobe Cable Car, and Kanden Tunnel Electric Bus.

The price of a pass for a specific route is the sum of the fares for all transportation on that route, with no discount. However, if you purchase a round-trip ticket, there is a discount. For example, a one-way ticket from Tateyama Station to Kurobe Lake costs 9,140 yen, while a round-trip ticket costs 16,480 yen, which is about a 10% discount compared to two one-way tickets.

### 1\. Fares for Various Transportation on the Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route

After significant price increases in 2022 and 2023, the fares for the Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route did not increase again from 2024. The fares for 2026 are the same as those in 2023. Below are the one-way fares for various transportation on the Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route in 2026: (The blue numbers in the image are adult fares, and the red numbers are child fares for ages 6-11. Children under 6 are free.)

![Tateyama Kurobe Transportation Fees](https://www.travelclassroom.net/eng/wp-content/uploads/folder01/ateyama-Kurobe-Alpine-Route_2023Fare_01.jpg)

Below are the round-trip fares for various transportation on the Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route in 2026:

![Tateyama Kurobe Transportation Fees](https://www.travelclassroom.net/eng/wp-content/uploads/folder01/ateyama-Kurobe-Alpine-Route_2023Fare_02.jpg)

Below are the ticket prices for several main itineraries in 2026 (adult fares):

- Dentetsu Toyama Station ~ Ogizawa Station \[Ogizawa Station ~ Dentetsu Toyama Station\] one-way ticket – 12,170 yen
- Tateyama Station ~ Ogizawa Station \[Ogizawa Station ~ Tateyama Station\] one-way ticket – 10,940 yen
- Dentetsu Toyama Station ~ Kurobe Lake round-trip ticket – 18,940 yen
- Tateyama Station ~ Kurobe Lake round-trip ticket – 16,480 yen
- Ogizawa Station ~ Murodo round-trip ticket – 12,300 yen

To check the fares for the Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route:

- [Japanese Version](https://www.alpen-route.com/access_new/fare/person/)
- [English Version](https://www.alpen-route.com/en/fare/)

### 2\. Passes Including JR, Bus, and Tateyama Kurobe Tickets

In addition to purchasing individual tickets for various transportation on the Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route, you can also purchase some transportation passes that include JR train tickets, express bus tickets, and Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route tickets from major cities such as Nagoya, Osaka, and Tokyo to Tateyama Kurobe.

For example, the “Alpine-Takayama-Matsumoto Area Tourist Pass”, “Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route Shinjuku Ticket” and “Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Free Pass.” For detailed information about these passes, please refer to the later section “ [Purchasing and Using JR Passes Including Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route Tickets](https://www.travelclassroom.net/eng/alpine-ticket.html#pass).”

## How to Purchase Tickets for Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route Transportation

There are two main methods to purchase tickets for the Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route transportation. The first method is to purchase tickets on the day at the station ticket office. The second method is to pre-purchase tickets through the official website of the Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route and then print the tickets at the self-service ticket machines at the station on the day or the day before. Below is a detailed explanation of these two methods.

### 1\. Purchasing Tickets at the Station on the Day

Tickets for the Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route transportation can be purchased at the ticket offices at each station. If you are ascending from the Toyama Prefecture side, you can purchase tickets at the Toyama Chihou Railway Toyama Station (Dentetsu Toyama Station) or Tateyama Station. If you are ascending from the Nagano Prefecture side, you can purchase tickets at Ogizawa Station. Each station on the Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route has a ticket office where you can purchase tickets for the same day.

![Tateyama Kurobe Pass](https://www.travelclassroom.net/eng/wp-content/uploads/folder01/Tateyama-Kurobe-Alpine-Route_Ticket-Office.jpg)

Below are the ticket counter hours at Toyama Chitetsu Station (Dentetsu Toyama Station) for purchasing and exchanging tickets for Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route transportation. The [business hours](https://www.chitetsu.co.jp/?page_id=817) are from 07:30 to 11:00. On special dates, the hours will be extended to 05:00 or 06:00.

Below are the operating hours for special days in 2026:

- April 15–16, April 25–26, May 2–5, 2026: from 4:40 AM
- April 17–24, April 27–May 1, May 6–15, 2026: from 6:30 AM

![Tateyama Kurobe Transportation Pass](https://www.travelclassroom.net/eng/wp-content/uploads/folder01/Tateyama-Kurobe-Alpine-Route_Ticket-Office_01.jpg)![Tateyama Kurobe Transportation Pass](https://www.travelclassroom.net/eng/wp-content/uploads/folder01/Tateyama-Kurobe-Alpine-Route_Ticket-Office_02.jpg)![Tateyama Kurobe Transportation Pass](https://www.travelclassroom.net/eng/wp-content/uploads/folder01/Tateyama-Kurobe-Alpine-Route_Ticket-Office_03.jpg)

Below is the location of the ticket counter at Tateyama Station. The counter opens 20 minutes before the departure of the first Tateyama Cable Car.

![Tateyama Kurobe Pass](https://www.travelclassroom.net/eng/wp-content/uploads/folder01/Tateyama-Kurobe-Alpine-Route_Ticket-Office_04.jpg)![Tateyama Kurobe Pass](https://www.travelclassroom.net/eng/wp-content/uploads/folder01/Tateyama-Kurobe-Alpine-Route_Ticket-Office_05.jpg)![Tateyama Kurobe Pass](https://www.travelclassroom.net/eng/wp-content/uploads/folder01/Tateyama-Kurobe-Alpine-Route_Ticket-Office_06.jpg)

Below is the location of the ticket office at Ogizawa Station:

![Tateyama Kurobe Pass](https://www.travelclassroom.net/eng/wp-content/uploads/folder01/Tateyama-Kurobe-Alpine-Route_Ticket-Office_07.jpg)![Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route Ticket](https://www.travelclassroom.net/eng/wp-content/uploads/folder01/Tateyama-Kurobe-Alpine-Route_Ticket-Office_08.jpg)

[Klook.com](https://www.klook.com/)

Please note that when purchasing tickets at the station ticket office, you can only buy tickets departing from that station. For example, you cannot buy tickets departing from Tateyama Station at Toyama Station; you can only buy tickets departing from Toyama Station.

Additionally, not all station ticket offices sell tickets to all destinations. For example, Dentetsu Toyama Station does not sell tickets to Daikanbo or round-trip tickets to Ogizawa Station. Below is a chart showing the types of tickets available at each station:

![Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route Ticket](https://www.travelclassroom.net/eng/wp-content/uploads/folder01/station-ticket-office.png)

Additionally, the Tateyama Cable Car from Tateyama Station to Bijodaira and the Kanden Tunnel Electric Bus from Ogizawa Station to Kurobe Damrequire reserved seating times. However, when purchasing tickets at the station ticket office, you can only reserve seating times for the same day. Therefore, even if you arrive in Toyama City the day before your Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route tour, you cannot purchase tickets for the next day in advance.

Apart from the Tateyama Cable Car from Tateyama Station to Bijodaira and the Kanden Tunnel Electric Bus from Ogizawa Station to Kurobe Dam, which require reserved seating times, other transportation methods do not require reserved seating times.

You just need to queue at the station as instructed, and the tickets are valid for 5 days from the date of issue (for one-time use only, not unlimited rides). Therefore, even if you stay overnight on Tateyama and descend the next day, you can still use the ticket.

Below are the tickets (boarding passes) purchased at the station ticket office:

![Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route Ticket](https://www.travelclassroom.net/eng/wp-content/uploads/folder01/Tateyama-Kurobe-Alpine-Route_Ticket.jpg)

### 2\. Purchasing Tickets in Advance on the Official Website

In addition to purchasing tickets upon arrival at the station, tickets for various transportation methods on the Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route can also be purchased through the official online ticketing system ( [Tateyama Kurobe Alpen Route WEB Ticket](https://tateyama-kurobe-webservice.jp/AlpenTour/html/VW001W0010.html)).

Among the various transportation methods on the Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route, only the Tateyama Cable Car from Tateyama Station to Bijodaira and the Kanden Tunnel Electric Bus from Ogizawa Station to Kurobe Dam require reserved seating times. The Tateyama Cable Car from Bijodaira to Tateyama Station, the Kanden Tunnel Electric Bus from Kurobe Dam to Ogizawa Station, and other transportation methods do not require reserved seating times.

Therefore, when touring the Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route, only one ride requires a reserved seating time. If you are ascending from Tateyama Station, the reserved seating time is for the Tateyama Cable Car from Tateyama Station to Bijodaira. If you are ascending from Ogizawa Station, the reserved seating time is for the Kanden Tunnel Electric Bus from Ogizawa Station to Kurobe Dam.

Since more people ascend from Tateyama Station, the Tateyama Cable Car from Tateyama Station to Bijodaira is generally more heavily booked, and the cable car has limited capacity. Therefore, on weekends and holidays during the peak season, it often gets fully booked early. On the other hand, fewer people ascend from Ogizawa Station, and the Kanden Tunnel Electric Bus has a larger capacity, so there are usually seats available on the Kanden Tunnel Electric Bus from Ogizawa Station to Kurobe Dam.

If there are no available seats for online reservations, it does not necessarily mean that the ride is fully booked, as a portion of seats are reserved for on-the-spot sales on the day. Therefore, even if there are no seats available online, you may still be able to purchase tickets at the station on the day. Additionally, only regular rides are available for online booking, but during the peak season, there are usually extra rides that are not available for online booking, so you can generally purchase tickets for these at the station.

In summary, if you want to plan your trip more securely, you can purchase tickets and reserve seating times for the Tateyama Cable Car or Kanden Tunnel Electric Bus in advance online. However, even if you cannot reserve your desired time, there is no need to worry. Arriving early at the station (Toyama Station, Tateyama Station, or Ogizawa Station) on the day will allow you to purchase tickets and board the Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route.

\[Note\]: When registering for an account, you can switch the webpage to different languages such as Japanese, Traditional Chinese, Simplified Chinese, English, Korean, Thai, Vietnamese, Indonesian, German, and French. If you register using the Japanese version, you need to fill in your name in Katakana, whereas the foreign language versions do not require this. ##### (2) Purchasing Tickets

After registering an account, you can log in to the [Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route Online Ticket System](https://tateyama-kurobe-webservice.jp/AlpenTour/html/VW001W0010.html) to purchase tickets for the Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route. The specific steps are as follows:

【Note】: The Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route online ticket purchase system should normally allow switching from the Japanese version to a foreign language version. However, starting from 2024, after logging into your member account, the system only displays the Japanese version, with no button visible to switch to a foreign language version, making it impossible to switch to Chinese or English. Therefore, when purchasing tickets, you can only use the Japanese version.

\[Step 1\] On the Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route Online Ticket System webpage, click on the “My Page” button at the top right corner. Then enter your account email and password, and click “Log in” to access the system. (Note: You can still use the foreign language version before logging in.)

![Tateyama Kurobe Ticket](https://www.travelclassroom.net/eng/wp-content/uploads/folder01/alpine-web-ticket-09.jpg)

\[Step 2\] Click on “Make a new reservation” (新規予約はこちら). (Note: If a small confirmation window appears afterwards, click “新規予約はこちら” again.)

![Tateyama Kurobe Ticket](https://www.travelclassroom.net/eng/wp-content/uploads/folder01/alpine-web-ticket-10.jpg)

\[Step 3\] Select the travel date.

![Tateyama Kurobe online ticket purchase - select date](https://www.travelclassroom.net/wp-content/uploads/2018/03/alpine-web-ticket-update-02.webp)

\[Step 4\] Select the departure station, arrival station, and route type (片道 (One-way) or 往復 (Round-trip)). (Note: This is for purchasing advance tickets for the route section only, so only 片道 (One-way) is available for selection here. Additionally, under normal sales conditions, the available departure and arrival stations would differ, but currently only Toyama and Ogizawa can be selected.)

![Tateyama Kurobe online ticket purchase - select route](https://www.travelclassroom.net/wp-content/uploads/2018/03/alpine-web-ticket-update-03.webp)

\[Step 5\] After setting the above options, images of the available products will appear. Click on the product image, then select the desired boarding time slot and the specific boarding time. (Note: The boarding time refers to the departure time for either the Tateyama Cable Car from Tateyama Station to Bijodaira or the Kanden Tunnel Electric Bus from Ogizawa Station to Kurobe Dam.)

![Tateyama Kurobe online ticket purchase - select boarding time](https://www.travelclassroom.net/wp-content/uploads/2018/03/alpine-web-ticket-update-04.webp)

\[Step 6\] Specify the number of passengers. (Note: Individuals aged 12 or older need to purchase adult tickets (おとな（中学生以上）). Children aged 6-11 purchase child tickets (こども（小学生）). Children under 6 are free of charge and do not need to be selected in the passenger count.)

![Tateyama Kurobe online ticket purchase - select number of passengers](https://www.travelclassroom.net/wp-content/uploads/2018/03/alpine-web-ticket-update-05.webp)

\[Step 7\] Choose whether to add [bus tickets](https://www.alpen-route.com/_wp/webticket_op1-1) from Ogizawa Station to Shinano-Omachi Station or Nagano Station. Leave it blank if not needed. After making your selection, click “ご予約内容の確認” (Confirm Reservation Details).

![Tateyama Kurobe online ticket purchase - add-on tickets](https://www.travelclassroom.net/wp-content/uploads/2018/03/alpine-web-ticket-update-06.webp)

\[Note\]: Bus tickets purchased through the online ticket system for the [route bus between Ogizawa Station and Shinano-Omachi Station](https://www.alpico.co.jp/traffic/local/hakuba/ogizawa/) and the [express bus between Ogizawa Station and Nagano Station](https://www.alpico.co.jp/traffic/express/nagano_omachi/) cannot be refunded after purchase. However, the number of passengers can be reduced, but refunds can only be processed at the Ogizawa Station ticket office. When boarding the bus, you will need to present the electronic ticket from the online ticket system or a printed copy of the electronic ticket. For more details, please refer to [this webpage](https://www.alpen-route.com/_wp/webticket_op1-2). Additionally, bus tickets purchased here cannot be used for intermediate stops.

![Tateyama Kurobe Ticket](https://www.travelclassroom.net/eng/wp-content/uploads/folder01/alpine-web-ticket-13.jpg)

Note: The image above is from the official website tutorial.

[Klook.com](https://www.klook.com/)

\[Step 8\] After confirming that the ticket information is correct, click “Enter payment information” to proceed to payment.

![Tateyama Kurobe Ticket](https://www.travelclassroom.net/eng/wp-content/uploads/folder01/alpine-web-ticket-14.jpg)

\[Step 9\] Enter your credit card information, including the credit card number (Credit card number), expiration date (Expiration date), and security code (CSC). Then click “Confirm payment information” to complete the payment.

![Tateyama Kurobe Ticket](https://www.travelclassroom.net/eng/wp-content/uploads/folder01/alpine-web-ticket-15.jpg)

After successfully purchasing the ticket, the ticket information will be displayed, including a QR Code. You can scan this QR Code at the self-service ticket machine at the station to collect your ticket. You can print this page, save a screenshot on your phone, or log in to the online ticket system on your phone to display the QR Code when collecting your ticket.

![Tateyama Kurobe Ticket](https://www.travelclassroom.net/eng/wp-content/uploads/folder01/alpine-web-ticket-16.jpg)

Note: The image above is from the official website tutorial.

##### (3) Changing Tickets

After purchasing tickets online, the only content that can be changed online is the number of passengers. You can log in to the [Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route Online Ticket System](https://tateyama-kurobe-webservice.jp/AlpenTour/html/VW001W0010.html) to change the number of passengers (increase or decrease the number) before 2:59 PM the day before the ticket date (Japan time).

If you increase the number of passengers, you will need to pay for the additional tickets. If you decrease the number of passengers, the refund for the reduced tickets will be credited back to the credit card used for the purchase. Changing the number of passengers through the online ticket system before the deadline does not incur a handling fee.

To change the number of passengers, log in to the online ticket system and go to My Page. Click on “Confirm reservation“, then click “Change” in the displayed ticket record to make changes.

![Tateyama Kurobe Ticket](https://www.travelclassroom.net/eng/wp-content/uploads/folder01/alpine-web-ticket-17.jpg)

After the deadline (2:59 PM the day before the ticket date), you cannot change the number of passengers through the online ticket system. However, if you have not yet collected the ticket, you can make changes at the ticket counter at the station (Tateyama Station, Ogizawa Station, or Dentetsu Toyama Station) on the day of travel. At the ticket counter, in addition to changing the number of passengers, you can also change the departure time (for the Tateyama Cable Car from Tateyama Station to Bijodaira or the Kanden Tunnel Electric Bus from Ogizawa Station to Kurobe Dam).

Even if the original departure time has passed, you can still make changes as long as the ticket has not been collected, but the new departure time must be on the same day as the original ticket. Changing the number of passengers or departure time at the station ticket counter incurs a handling fee of 500 yen per ticket.

Additionally, please note that bus tickets purchased through the Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route Online Ticket System for the route bus between Ogizawa Station and Shinano-Omachi Station and the express bus between Ogizawa Station and Nagano Station cannot be refunded. Refunds for reducing the number of passengers can only be processed at the Ogizawa Station ticket office.

##### (4) Canceling Tickets

Tickets for the Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route purchased online can be canceled through the [online ticketing system](https://tateyama-kurobe-webservice.jp/AlpenTour/html/VW001W0010.html). Cancellations made before 2:59 PM (Japan Time) on the day before the ticket date are free of charge. If canceled after this deadline but before the departure time (the Tateyama Cable Car from Tateyama Station to Bijodaira or the Kanden Tunnel Electric Bus from Ogizawa Station to Kurobe Dam), a 500 yen fee per ticket will be charged. Cancellations are not possible after the departure time.

However, tickets purchased during the advance sale period, have special cancellation rules. If canceled 10 days before the travel date, no fee is charged. If canceled after this period, a 1,000 yen fee per ticket will be charged.

To cancel a ticket, log in to the online ticketing system, go to My Page, click on “Confirm reservation“, and then click “Cancel” on the displayed ticket record to proceed with the cancellation.

![Tateyama Kurobe Ticket](https://www.travelclassroom.net/eng/wp-content/uploads/folder01/alpine-web-ticket-18.jpg)

Note: The above image is from the official website tutorial.

##### 5\. Ticket Pickup

After purchasing Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route tickets online, you need to collect the physical paper tickets before use. Tickets can be picked up from 12:00 PM (noon) on the day before the travel date. Physical tickets can be printed from self-service ticket machines at Tateyama Station, Ogizawa Station, and Toyama Station of the Toyama Chihou Railway. To print the ticket, simply scan the QR code from the ticket record on the machine and confirm on the screen to print the ticket.

![Tateyama Kurobe Ticket](https://www.travelclassroom.net/eng/wp-content/uploads/folder01/alpine-web-ticket-19.jpg)![Tateyama Kurobe Ticket](https://www.travelclassroom.net/eng/wp-content/uploads/folder01/alpine-web-ticket-20.jpg)

Note: The above image is from the official website tutorial.

Below are the locations of the self-service ticket machines at Tateyama Station, Ogizawa Station, and Toyama Station of the Toyama Chihou Railway (official website tutorial images).

![Tateyama Kurobe Ticket](https://www.travelclassroom.net/eng/wp-content/uploads/folder01/alpine-web-ticket-21.jpg)![Tateyama Kurobe Ticket](https://www.travelclassroom.net/eng/wp-content/uploads/folder01/alpine-web-ticket-22.jpg)![Tateyama Kurobe Ticket](https://www.travelclassroom.net/eng/wp-content/uploads/folder01/alpine-web-ticket-23.jpg)

Self-service ticket machines are only available during station operating hours. The self-service ticket machines at Dentetsu Toyama Station can be used from 5:00 AM to 11:30 PM.

## Purchasing and Using JR Passes Including Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route Tickets

In addition to purchasing individual tickets for the various transportation options on the Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route, there are also several passes available that include transportation on the Alpine Route as well as JR trains and buses connecting nearby major cities.

Examples include the “Alpine-Takayama-Matsumoto Area Tourist Pass“, the “Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Free Pass“, and the “Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route Shinjuku Ticket“. If you are not driving to Tateyama Kurobe, purchasing these JR Passes or package tickets can generally save you a significant amount of money.

### 1\. Alpine-Takayama-Matsumoto Area Tourist Pass

The “ [Alpine-Takayama-Matsumoto Area Tourist Pass](https://touristpass.jp/en/alpine/)” is a JR Pass jointly offered by JR Central and JR West. This pass allows unlimited rides on the eight types of transportation on the Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route during its validity period, as well as unlimited rides on JR trains between Nagoya and Toyama, and between Nagoya and Shinano-Omachi.

![Tateyama Kurobe JR Pass](https://www.travelclassroom.net/eng/wp-content/uploads/folder01/Alpine-JR-Pass_en.jpg)

The specific areas covered by the “Alpine-Takayama-Matsumoto Area Tourist Pass” include:

- JR trains between Nagoya and Toyama via the Tokaido Main Line (Nagoya to Gifu) and the Takayama Main Line, including limited express, express, rapid, and local trains (ordinary cars only, no Green Car). Stops include Gifu, Mino, Gero Onsen, Takayama, and Hida Furukawa.
- JR trains between Nagoya and Shinano-Omachi via the Chuo Main Line (Nagoya to Shiojiri), the Shinonoi Line (Shiojiri to Kitamatsumoto), and the Oito Line (Kitamatsumoto to Shinano-Omachi), including limited express, express, rapid, and local trains (ordinary cars only, no Green Car). Stops include Ena Gorge, Narai, and Matsumoto.
- Trains on the Toyama Chihou Railway between Toyama and Tateyama Station, including limited express, rapid, and local trains (non-reserved seats only).
- Route buses between Ogizawa Station and Shinano-Omachi, passing through Omachi Onsen.
- Six types of mountain transportation on the Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route between Tateyama Station and Ogizawa Station (Tateyama Cable Car, Tateyama Highland Bus, Tateyama Tunnel Trolleybus, Tateyama Ropeway, Kurobe Cable Car, and Kanden Tunnel Electric Bus).

For more detailed information on the “Alpine-Takayama-Matsumoto Area Tourist Pass”, please refer to the article “ [Alpine-Takayama-Matsumoto Area Tourist Pass: Purchase, Exchange, Usage, and Riding Guide](https://www.travelclassroom.net/eng/alpine-pass.html)“.

### 2\. JR Central “Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Free Pass”

The “ [Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Free Pass](https://railway.jr-central.co.jp/tickets/tateyama-kurobe-alpine/)” is a domestic version for Japanese residents offered by JR Central, similar to the “ [Alpine-Takayama-Matsumoto Area Tourist Pass](https://www.travelclassroom.net/eng/alpine-pass.html).”

The coverage area, validity period, and price of the “Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Free Pass” are exactly the same as the “Alpine-Takayama-Matsumoto Area Tourist Pass,” but there are slight differences in the usage period, purchase period, sales channels, and how it is used.

Here are the basic details of the “Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Free Pass“:

- Coverage: Exactly the same as the coverage of the Alpine-Takayama-Matsumoto Area Tourist Pass;
- Validity: 5 consecutive days, same as the validity of the Alpine-Takayama-Matsumoto Area Tourist Pass;
- Price: Adults 24,500 yen, Children 12,250 yen, same as the price of the Alpine-Takayama-Matsumoto Area Tourist Pass;
- Usage Period: April 15 to November 30, 2026, but not valid during April 27 – May 6 and August 10 – 19;
- Sales Period: March 15 to November 26, 2026. Tickets can only be purchased one month before the start date of use;
- Purchase Channel: [JR West’s “e5489” online booking site](https://tickets.jr-odekake.net/shohindb/view/consumer/tokutoku/ticket.html?staticShnId=100022957);
- Ticket Collection Method: At JR Central station ticket offices or at designated ticket vending machines marked “5489サービス” located outside the ticket gates.

Note: Before 2026, the “Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Free Pass” was called the “ [Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Pass](https://jr-central.co.jp/news/release/_pdf/nws000001_00061.pdf).” It underwent a major revision starting in 2026.

Reference:

- [JR Central official website page for Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Free Pass](https://railway.jr-central.co.jp/tickets/tateyama-kurobe-alpine/)

For a detailed guide on the “Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Free Pass,” please refer to this article: [Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Free Pass: How to Buy, Pick Up, and Ride](https://www.travelclassroom.net/eng/tateyama-kurobe-alpine-free-pass.html).

### 3\. “Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route Shinjuku Ticket”

The “ [Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route Shinjuku Ticket](https://highway-buses.jp/ticket/alpineroute-shinjuku.php)” is a discount package for the Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route offered by Keio Dentetsu Bus.

The package includes a one-way highway bus ticket from Tokyo’s Shinjuku Station to Shinano-Omachi Station (or Ogizawa Station) in Nagano Prefecture, a route bus ticket from Shinano-Omachi Station to Ogizawa Station (included only in the daytime bus package), and one-way tickets for the seven transportation modes on the Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route from Ogizawa Station to Toyama Chihō Railway’s Toyama Station.

These modes include the Kanden Tunnel Electric Bus, Kurobe Cable Car, Tateyama Ropeway, Tateyama Tunnel Electric Bus, Tateyama Highland Bus, Tateyama Cable Car, and Toyama Chihō Railway.

![Tateyama Kurobe Ticket](https://www.travelclassroom.net/eng/wp-content/uploads/folder01/alpine-route-shinjuku-02.jpg)

The “Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route Shinjuku Ticket” is divided into two types, “Overnight Bus” and “Daytime Bus,” based on the departure time of the highway bus from Shinjuku Station to Ogizawa Station.

For the “Overnight Bus” type, the highway bus from Shinjuku Station to Ogizawa Station is an overnight sleeper bus. It departs at 11:15 PM and arrives at Ogizawa Station at 5:32 AM. You can start your mountain journey the same day, but you might be tired due to lack of sleep. Also, please note that the overnight highway bus from Shinjuku Station to Ogizawa Station does not run every day, and according to the website information, the overnight bus is currently suspended.

For the “Daytime Bus” type, the highway bus runs during the day with 2 to 3 services daily. However, the daytime highway bus only goes as far as Shinano-Omachi. The journey takes about 4.5 hours, arriving in Shinano-Omachi in the afternoon or evening. To go from Shinano-Omachi to Ogizawa Station, you need to take a route bus. The package includes the ticket for the route bus from Shinano-Omachi to Ogizawa Station. This bus ticket is valid for two days, allowing you to get off midway, making it convenient to stay overnight in Shinano-Omachi or the nearby Omachi Onsen area before heading up the mountain.

Here are the tickets included in the “Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route Shinjuku Ticket”:

- Daytime Bus: One-way highway bus ticket from Tokyo Shinjuku Station to Shinano-Omachi Station (Nagano Prefecture) + Route bus ticket from Shinano-Omachi Station to Ogizawa Station (valid for 2 days, allowing boarding/alighting midway) + One-way tickets for the seven transportation modes on the Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route from Ogizawa Station to Toyama Chihō Railway’s Toyama Station (Kanden Tunnel Electric Bus, Kurobe Cable Car, Tateyama Ropeway, Tateyama Tunnel Electric Bus, Tateyama Highland Bus, Tateyama Cable Car, and Toyama Chihō Railway), valid for 5 days.
- Overnight Bus: One-way highway bus ticket from Tokyo Shinjuku Station to Ogizawa Station (Nagano Prefecture) + One-way tickets for the seven transportation modes on the Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route from Ogizawa Station to Toyama Chihō Railway’s Toyama Station (Kanden Tunnel Electric Bus, Kurobe Cable Car, Tateyama Ropeway, Tateyama Tunnel Electric Bus, Tateyama Highland Bus, Tateyama Cable Car, and Toyama Chihō Railway), valid for 5 days.

The price for the “Daytime Bus” version of the “Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route Shinjuku Ticket” is 19,000 yen (Children 9,500 yen). The “Overnight Bus” version is about 400 yen more expensive. The regular price for the Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route tickets from Ogizawa Station to Toyama Station is 12,170 yen, and the regular highway bus fare from Shinjuku Station to Ogizawa Station is 7,500 yen, totaling 19,670 yen. Therefore, purchasing the “Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route Shinjuku Ticket” saves you about 670 yen.

## What’s the Weather Like at Tateyama Kurobe? Where Can I Find Live Cams?

Tateyama Kurobe features a classic high-mountain climate.

The highest point, **Murodo Station**, sits at a staggering 2,450 meters above sea level. That means the temperature difference between the mountains and the lowlands is often between 10°C and 15°C.

Even in the middle of summer when the plains are melting, the mountains stay a cool and comfortable 10°C to 20°C, though it can get quite chilly in the mornings and evenings.

High-altitude weather is also famously fickle; one second it’s sunny, and the next you’re surrounded by clouds or rain.

## Tateyama Kurobe Seasonal Itineraries

Starting every December, the entire mountain is blanketed in heavy ice and snow due to the harsh winter, leading to a closure that lasts several months. The route doesn’t reopen to visitors until **mid-April** of the following year.

So, if you want to catch a glimpse of the Tateyama peaks, you’ll need to plan your trip during the open seasons of spring, summer, or autumn.

| **Season** | **Mountain Conditions** |
| --- | --- |
| **Winter to Spring (Starting December)** | Closed Period |
| **Spring to Summer (April – June)** | Snow Wall Season |
| **Summer (June – October)** | Dam Sightseeing Discharge |
| **Autumn (September – Early November)** | Autumn Foliage Season |

### Spring: April to June

When the mountain first opens in April, the snow walls are at their most spectacular, reaching heights of up to 20 meters.

The snow gradually melts through July, so by June, the walls stand at about 10 meters, while fresh green sprouts begin to peek through.

![The crystal clear Mikurigaike Pond reflects the snow-dusted peaks of Mt. Tateyama under a vibrant blue sky.](https://www.kkday.com/en/blog/wp-content/uploads/Tateyama-Kurobe-warm-weather-1.webp)Stunning reflection of the Japanese Alps in the calm Mikurigaike Pond (via KKday Supplier)

### Summer: June to October

Summer is the perfect time for hiking and mountaineering. The temperatures are refreshingly cool, and you might even spot special local wildlife like the Rock Ptarmigan or the Japanese Serow.

This season also marks the start of the sightseeing water discharge at the dam. It’s the absolute best time to admire Kurobe Dam and Mikuriga-ike Pond. And depending on the mountain conditions, these views can sometimes last into October.

### Autumn: September to November

Tateyama’s autumn foliage is famous for its distinct layers of colour that change with the altitude.

Starting in September, the leaves at the summit begin turning red. By October, the entire mountainside is a vibrant tapestry; you’ll see a stunning gradient of yellow, orange, red, and green stretching from the top down to the base.

Tateyama Kurobe is one of the world’s most impressive heavy-snowfall regions.

Head to the route’s highest point, Murodo, to experience the ultimate visual and tactile thrill as you walk within a breathtaking 500-meter-long corridor of towering snow walls.

### Tateyama Kurobe Must-See: Kurobe Dam (Kurobe Reservoir)

Kurobe Dam is one of the most popular attractions in the entire Tateyama Kurobe area. Every time the water is released, it surges against the surrounding walls with incredible power, often refracting the light to create beautiful rainbows.

Surrounded by the majestic Tateyama peaks, known as the Northern Alps, it has become an absolute must-visit spot for seasoned Japanese backpackers.

![A high-angle view of the Kurobe Dam in Japan, showcasing its massive curved concrete structure and a powerful water discharge into the valley below.](https://www.kkday.com/en/blog/wp-content/uploads/Kurobe-dam.webp)The impressive Kurobe Dam releasing water amidst the scenic Japanese Alps (via KKday Supplier)

Located in Toyama Prefecture, Kurobe Dam sits in a region with such steep terrain and harsh, snowy winters that it was once completely inaccessible.

The original construction was a massive and difficult undertaking that sadly resulted in many casualties. As a result, the story of its creation has been frequently adapted into movies and TV dramas, giving the dam a special place in the hearts of Japanese people.

Today, Kurobe Dam serves a vital role, supplying a huge amount of electricity to the entire Kansai region.

## How Should You Arrange Your Tateyama Kurobe Climbing Route?

The stretch from Tateyama Station in Toyama Prefecture to Ogizawa Station in Nagano Prefecture is known as the **Alpen Route**. This is the Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route that cuts right through the heart of the Japanese Alps.

![A group of tourists walking along an asphalt road carved between towering, vertical walls of white snow.](https://www.kkday.com/en/blog/wp-content/uploads/alpine-route-with-hikers.webp)Tourists walking through the spectacular towering snow walls of Tateyama Kurobe (via KKday Supplier)

Since you’ll be crossing rugged natural terrain, you’ll get to experience six different modes of transport along the way.

A full traverse from Tateyama to Ogizawa takes about 6 to 8 hours.

If you go from Tateyama to Kurobe Dam and head back, plan for 8 to 9 hours.

Alternatively, going from Ogizawa to Murodo (the Snow Walls) and back takes around 5 to 7 hours.

A 1-way trip from Tateyama to Ogizawa costs over 10,000 yen. It’s a great idea to research exactly which spots you want to visit to find the best way to save some yen.

### Alpen Route Transport Modes:

- **Tateyama to Bijodaira:** Tateyama Cable Car
- **Bijodaira to Murodo:** Highland Bus
- **Murodo to Daikanbo:** Tateyama Tunnel Trolley Bus
- **Daikanbo to Kurobedaira:** Tateyama Ropeway
- **Kurobedaira to Kurobe Lake:** Kurobe Cable Car
- **Kurobe Dam to Ogizawa:** Kanden Tunnel Electric Bus

## How Do You Get to Tateyama Kurobe? Tateyama Kurobe Transport Guide

Before diving into the logistics, your first step is deciding whether to start your mountain ascent from the Tateyama side or the Ogizawa side.

Generally speaking, if you are starting from Kyoto or Osaka, you’ll likely head to Toyama first and enter via Tateyama.

If you are coming from Tokyo, you’ll head to Shinano-Omachi and enter via Ogizawa.

For those starting in Nagoya, which is the most common starting point, you have the luxury of choosing either direction!

### Tateyama Kurobe Route 1: Tokyo – Tateyama Kurobe – Osaka

The Hokuriku Arch Pass bridges JR East and JR West, allowing travellers to visit Tokyo, Osaka, and the Hokuriku region all in one go.

You get seven consecutive days of unlimited rides on the Hokuriku Shinkansen, plus the N’EX (from Tokyo airports to the city) and the Haruka Express (from Osaka to Kansai Airport).

![Karuizawa Prince Ski Resort A skier in a bright green jacket and orange pants carves down a snowy slope at a ski resort.](https://www.kkday.com/en/blog/wp-content/uploads/Karuizawa-Prince-Hotel-Ski-Resort-03-2.webp)A skier enjoys a scenic downhill run with mountain views (via KKday Supplier)

You can even use it on JR lines within the Tokyo and Osaka city limits.

Since it covers super popular spots like Karuizawa, Kanazawa, and Toyama along the Hokuriku Shinkansen line, it is an incredibly great deal.

### Tateyama Kurobe Route 2: Nagoya – Tateyama Kurobe – Nagoya

Nagoya is the gateway to the Hokuriku region.

If you want to visit Nagoya, Shirakawa-go, and Tateyama Kurobe, and you’re the type of person who loves planning your own path, Route 2 is a fantastic way to save money while having a blast.

While JR Central issues only four types of PASSes, which is quite a bit fewer than JR East or JR West, it offers a huge variety of special ticket sets.

The set our editors are introducing today is perfect for those planning a full traverse of the Alpine Route. You get unlimited rides back and forth on the Alpine Route.

There are two types: the Hida Course and the Shirasagi Course. Both start in Nagoya, but the stops and transport methods along the way differ slightly.

#### Hida Course

Departing from Nagoya, you’ll take the JR Tokaido Line and Takayama Main Line through Gifu and Hida-Furukawa to Toyama, or take the JR Chuo Line to Matsumoto and transfer to Shinano-Omachi.

You must follow the loop in one direction and cannot backtrack. Then, hop off mid-journey at stations between Gifu and Hida-Furukawa, Shinano-Omachi and Matsumoto, and Seba and Nakatsugawa, but mid-journey stops are not allowed on other JR sections.

You can reserve seats on one Limited Express train for each leg (outbound and return), with free seating on other Limited Express trains. This pass also allows you to ride the Shinkansen between Shizuoka and Nagoya.

**Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route Map**

- **Validity:** 3 days
- **Purchase Locations:** All ticket offices at JR Nagoya Station and the Tourist Information Center at Chubu Centrair International Airport.
- **Capacity:** Up to 4 people. The more people you buy for, the cheaper it gets. But everyone must enter and exit the stations together.

#### Shirasagi Course

The Shirasagi Course, which also starts in Nagoya, is another popular pick.

This one takes you directly from Nagoya to Kanazawa, where you’ll transfer to the Hokuriku Shinkansen to Toyama (non-reserved seats only) to begin the Alpine Route. Just like the Hida Course, you must travel in one direction and can’t backtrack.

One key difference: unlike the Hida Course, this set does not include the Shinkansen between Shizuoka and Nagoya.

You can get off mid-journey between Shinano-Omachi and Matsumoto, and Seba and Nakatsugawa, but not on other JR sections.

**Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route Map**

- **Validity:** 3 days
- **Purchase Locations:** All ticket offices at JR Nagoya Station and the Tourist Information Centre at Chubu Centrair International Airport.
- **Capacity:** Up to 4 people. It gets cheaper the more people there are, but you must travel as a group!

#### JR Alpine-Takayama-Matsumoto Area Tourist Pass

In addition to the two Alpine Route ticket options mentioned above, you might consider the more flexible 5-day JR Alpine-Takayama-Matsumoto Area Tourist Pass. It’s a bit more versatile because there aren’t as many restrictions on where or how often you can get on and off the train.

Whether it’s the Gero Onsen, the historic streets of Takayama, the Tateyama Kurobe route itself, Matsumoto Castle, or the Hida area, this one ticket gets you to a ton of popular spots.

If you want to focus your fun on Central Japan, choosing the JR PASS that hits all these major hubs is the way to go.

#### Shoryudo 3-Day / 5-Day Highway Bus Ticket

The Shoryudo tickets are an absolute steal! They cover highway buses between Nagoya, Takayama, Shirakawa-go, Kanazawa, and Toyama, plus routes to Chubu Centrair International Airport and Komatsu Airport.

If you’re planning to visit Shirakawa-go, Kanazawa, or Kamikochi, the Shoryudo bus is likely your best bet, as the other passes we mentioned don’t cover these specific areas.

![A white Mitsubishi Fuso Meitetsu Bus parked in a lot under a clear sky.](https://www.kkday.com/en/blog/wp-content/uploads/Shoryudo-Bus-Pass.webp)A modern Meitetsu tour bus parked and ready for passenger travel (via KKday Supplier)

The only downside is that the Tateyama Kurobe section requires a separate fee. Because of that, we recommend travelers using this ticket explore halfway through the Tateyama Kurobe route and then head back to Toyama.

This way, you won’t have to worry about luggage forwarding, and you can easily head from Toyama to Hirayu after coming down the mountain.

The main difference between the 3-day and 5-day pass is that the 5-day version adds Gokayama, Shinhotaka, and Matsumoto. For travelers who want to see Tateyama Kurobe and Shirakawa-go while exploring Nagoya or the wider Central region, this really is a perfect fit!

- **Transport Combo:** JR Central Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Ticket OR Shoryudo 3/5-Day Pass + Tateyama Kurobe Option Ticket
- **Validity:** 8 consecutive days / 3 or 5 consecutive days (Shoryudo)

### Tateyama Kurobe Route 3: Osaka, Kyoto, Shirakawa-go, Takayama, and Toyama (Tateyama Kurobe)

![A couple holding hands runs through deep snow toward a traditional Japanese gassho-zukuri farmhouse in Shirakawa-go.](https://www.kkday.com/en/blog/wp-content/uploads/takayama.webp)A couple runs toward a snow-covered traditional farmhouse in a winter wonderland (via KKday Supplier)

**Takayama-Hokuriku Area Tourist Pass**

If you’re looking to travel all the way from Osaka and Kyoto through to Nagoya, our editors think this is the perfect pass for you.

It covers the Haruka Express from Kansai Airport to Osaka City (non-reserved seats), the JR Osaka Loop Line, the Hokuriku Shinkansen (between Kanazawa and Toyama), and JR trains heading toward Nagoya.

## Tateyama Kurobe FAQs

![A scenic view of the Kappa Bridge, a wooden suspension bridge crossing the turquoise Azusa River in Kamikochi, Japan.](https://www.kkday.com/en/blog/wp-content/uploads/Tateyama-Kurobe-Alpine-Route-and-Kamikochi-2-Day-Tour.webp)The iconic Kappa Bridge over the Azusa River with snowy mountain peaks (via KKday Supplier)

### When does the Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route open?

The mountain typically opens in mid-April and stays accessible until the end of November. The route is usually closed from December through March of the following year.

### Where is the famous Alpine Route located?

The stretch from Tateyama Station in Toyama Prefecture to Ogizawa Station in Nagano Prefecture is known as the **Alpen Route**.

This is the Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route that cuts right through the Northern Alps. Because it crosses such rugged natural terrain, you’ll need to use six different modes of transport to complete the journey.

### What are the must-visit spots at Tateyama Kurobe?

Don’t miss the iconic Snow Walls and Mikuriga-ike Pond at **Murodo Station**, the thundering Shomyu Falls at **Tateyama Station**, the magnificent **Kurobe Dam** (Kurobe Reservoir), and the relaxing **Omachi Onsen Village** at Ogizawa Station.
